label: early copy phase (delimiter + first ~3 outputs) of long sequences, sparse
explanation: Almost never fires in the original phase (5 of 12.9k dev activations). Fires at the <DEL> step (39% of mass, 5.2% rate) and on the first few copy steps (recall_idx 1-3, about 60% of mass), almost only in long sequences: rate rises steadily with L (0.2% at L=3-5, 1.9% at L=9; L>=7 holds about 91% of mass) and with outputs remaining (to_go=8 rate 7.8%). It goes quiet after recall_idx 4. The predicate (delimiter/copy, recall_idx<=3, L>=7) covers 87% of activations and 90% of mass, but only about 6% of matching steps fire, so token content clearly gates it. There is a token preference (k and w as inputs/first token, and sequences containing k/w/l), but conditioning on k/w/l only raises precision to about 9%, and no single token or position rule captured it. Magnitude: the top activations are at <DEL> or recall_idx 1-2 in L=8-9 sequences, often with input k or w. I did not find a clean magnitude rule beyond that.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=5: k, w, l, 2; t=6: k, w, l, 2; t=7: k, w, o, l) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: z, m, 1, n; delimiter step: g, 1, p, 2; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, recall_idx=1, L=3 & t=4.
